status_reviews.researcher_notes: REQUIRED annual-update status review for P0752 (Nord Stream 2 Gas Pipeline), with specific focus per task brief on: (1) the asymmetric damage between the two parallel lines, and (2) the Nord Stream 2 AG Swiss insolvency proceedings. FINDINGS: (1) Damage asymmetry -- the Sept 26, 2022 Baltic Sea sabotage ruptured three of the four Nord Stream lines; String A of Nord Stream 2 was one of the lines ruptured, while String B (the second NSP2 line) is widely reported as having survived largely intact/pressurized. This asymmetry does not change the row-level Status recommendation: GEM tracks NSP2 as a single two-line system, and even the reportedly-intact String B has never entered commercial operation (the German certification process that was the sole remaining approval step was suspended Feb 22, 2022, before the Sept 2022 sabotage even occurred) and has been kept deliberately offline/pressure-managed rather than activated -- the 2025 Danish Energy Agency permit for preservation/plugging measures covers exactly this kind of laid-up management of the undamaged line. So 'mothballed' (not 'operating' for String B, and not 'cancelled'/fully decommissioned for either line) remains the single most accurate status for the row as a whole. (2) Swiss insolvency -- Nord Stream 2 AG (Zug, Switzerland) has been in financial distress/insolvency-adjacent proceedings since the 2022 sanctions cut off its revenue prospects; 2025 Swiss court proceedings extended protection/restructuring time to the company rather than forcing full liquidation, meaning the corporate entity itself is being preserved (creditors including ENGIE, OMV, Shell, Uniper and Wintershall are engaging with a restructuring process rather than a winding-up), consistent with a dormant-but-not-terminated project posture. VERDICT: CONFIRM -- 'mothballed' remains the correct current status as of the most recent evidence located (2025-11-25). This is not being downgraded to 'shelved'/'cancelled' because neither line has been formally abandoned or decommissioned (the preservation/plugging measures are explicitly precautionary/maintenance in nature, and the Swiss corporate entity survives via restructuring rather than dissolution), and it is not being upgraded to 'operating' because no commercial gas flow has occurred or is authorized on either string. Given this is flagged in the task brief as the highest-stakes status judgment in the batch, the full evidence chain and dating are preserved here for a human reviewer to audit independently.
